extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent agents/attorneys, receiving Offices and International Authorities processing PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing, submitting and managing PCT international applications during the international phase (confidentiality, biological deposits, sequence listings, licensing indications, third‑party observations, successor states, and telecommunication/original document rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Annexes B before telecommunication submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should, before sending a document by a means of telecommunication, check in Annexes B to ascertain the applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the documents to be submitted are documents making up the international application or replacement sheets containing amendments or corrections to the international application, the original should in any event be mailed as a matter of course on the same or the following day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original accompanying letter for telecommunicated documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original is sent to an Office or organization of a document previously transmitted to that Office or organization by a means of telecommunication, the original must be accompanied by a letter identifying the date and means of the earlier transmission (Rule 92.4(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in the letter the date and means of earlier transmission to allow matching with the telecommunicated copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of illegible or incomplete telecommunication transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If part or all of a document received by such means of transmission is illegible, or if part of the document is not received, the document is treated as not having been received to the extent that it is illegible or that the attempted transmission failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office or organization promptly notifies the applicant accordingly; mailing the original promptly avoids problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and format of file reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or appointed agent may mark a file reference in the box provided on the first sheet of the request form and on other elements/correspondence; it may be letters, Arabic numerals or both, may use hyphen as separator and may not exceed 25 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office, the International Bureau, the ISA, the Authority specified for supplementary search and the IPEA will use the file reference in correspondence with the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality before international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application is confidential in relation to third parties until the international publication date, with only limited and specified exceptions (Articles 30 and 38; Rules 94.1(a), 94.1bis(a), 94.1ter(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau, the receiving Office and the ISA will, at the request of the applicant or any authorized person, furnish copies of any document in their file subject to reimbursement. A court order may substitute for applicant authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability after international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After international publication, the international application, published amendments under Article 19, the international search report and copies of priority documents are publicly available, subject to exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after 1 July 1998, the IB will furnish copies after publication upon reimbursement but will not provide access to documents omitted from international publication or prepared solely for internal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to omit information from public file access
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant can make a reasoned request to the International Bureau to omit certain information from public file access (Rule 94.1(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a request may be submitted at any time; when the IB omits information it will promptly notify other Offices/Authorities so they also do not provide access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international preliminary examination (IPE) files
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant requests international preliminary examination, the IB and the IPEA may not allow unauthorized access to the IPE file; access by third parties to IPE papers is permitted only if requested/authorized by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the international preliminary report on patentability and related documents have been communicated to each elected Office, third parties may gain access to these documents to the same extent as provided by national law. The IB may furnish copies to elected Offices on request; access is not provided to information omitted from publication or public access; furnishing copies may be subject to a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to include reference to deposited biological material
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT does not require inclusion of a reference to deposited biological material, but prescribes the contents of any reference and when such a reference must be furnished (Rule 13bis.1, Rule 48.2(a)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a reference only when required for disclosing the invention sufficiently for a person skilled in the art — i.e., where national law of any designated State requires making such a reference because biological material is not publicly available. Annex L lists Offices whose national law provides for such references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a PCT-compliant reference to deposited biological material
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to deposited biological material made in accordance with the requirements of the PCT must be regarded by each designated Office as satisfying the requirements of the national law applicable in that Office with regard to contents and time for furnishing (Rule 13bis.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the reference under PCT rules harmonizes compliance across designated Offices that have notified requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of deposited-material reference across designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference may be made for the purposes of all designated States or for one or only some of the designated States; it is considered made for all designated States unless expressly limited (Rule 13bis.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to different deposits may be made for different designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory indications in a deposited-material reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Indications specified by the PCT that must be given in a reference: (i) name and address of the depositary institution; (ii) date of the deposit; (iii) accession number given by that institution (Rule 13bis.3, Rule 12.1ter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex L sets out additional indications (if any) notified by national Offices; additional indications must be furnished in the filing language and in the translation language when a translation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indications concerning the biological material itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Some national laws require, besides deposit particulars, an indication concerning the biological material itself (e.g., short description of characteristics) to the extent information is available to the applicant (Rule 13bis.3(a)(iv), Rule 13bis.7(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements apply when the relevant Office is designated and has published the requirement; Annex L indicates which Offices have such requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for furnishing deposit indications (16‑month rule and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any indication is not included in the international application as filed, it may be furnished to the IB within 16 months from the priority date unless the IB has published that a designated Office requires earlier furnishing; indications furnished after 16 months but before technical preparations for publication are considered furnished on the last day of the 16‑month limit (Rule 13bis.4, Rule 13bis.7(a)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting early publication, furnish all indications by the time of the early publication request. Annex L specifies Offices with earlier time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to furnish deposit indications on time
rubrics_metrics.description: No check is made in the international phase to determine whether a reference has been furnished within the prescribed time limit; failure has no consequence if national law does not require the reference, and where there is a consequence it is the same as under the national law (Rule 13bis.3(b), Rule 13bis.4, Rule 48.2(a)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If indications were received after technical preparations for publication were completed, the IB notifies designated Offices of the dates on which indications were furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and placement for deposit references
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent deposit indications are not given in the description, they may be furnished on a separate sheet using Form PCT/RO/134; if submitted when filing, reference it in Checklist Box No. IX (Section 209).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain designated Offices require indications to be included in the description at filing, so the separate sheet may need to be included as part of the description. If furnished later it must be enclosed with a letter. Form PCT/RO/134 may be prepared using ePCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a depositary institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each national (or regional) Office that provides for deposits for patent procedure notifies the IB of depositary institutions permitted by its national law; the IB publishes this information in Official Notices (Annex L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Annex L or Official Notices to ensure deposit is made with an institution accepted by designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Offices cannot disregard a notified deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to a deposit cannot be disregarded by a designated Office for reasons pertaining to the depositary institution if the deposit was made with an institution notified by that Office (Rule 13bis.5(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By consulting Official Notices/Annex L applicants can ensure the deposit will be accepted by that designated Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISAs and IPEAs cannot require a sample for international processing
rubrics_metrics.description: International Searching Authorities and International Preliminary Examining Authorities may not require the furnishing of a sample of deposited biological material for purposes of international search or international preliminary examination (Rule 13bis.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for samples are governed by national laws in the national phase; do not expect ISAs/IPEAs to demand physical samples during international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of furnishing samples to third parties until national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 13bis.6 provides for delaying any furnishing of samples under national law in each designated Office until the start of the national phase, subject to ending events: (i) applicant has taken steps necessary to enter national phase before the designated Office; or (ii) international publication has the same effects as compulsory national publication and the international application qualifies for provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Contracting States whose laws provide provisional protection and the conditions required, refer to Annexes B. Some Offices (e.g., EPO) allow sample only to an expert nominated by requester until a certain event — see Annex L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special requirements for sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements apply to nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences disclosed in international applications (Rule 5.2, Rule 13ter, Section 208, Annex C of the Administrative Instructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the indicated paragraphs and Annex C and to National Phase provisions for national requirements; sequence listing rules and formats must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor State: definition and extension of effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A successor State is one whose territory was part of a predecessor PCT Contracting State and which has deposited a declaration indicating PCT applicability; as from that deposit date the successor State may be designated and the effects of certain international applications filed during a specified period are extended to the successor State (Rule 32.1(a),(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB publishes information in Official Notices about international applications whose effects are extended to a successor State and about time limits extended in relation to that State (Rule 32.1(c), Rule 32.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of extension to a successor State
rubrics_metrics.description: A successor State is considered designated in the international application on the international filing date; applicable time limits under Article 22 or 39(1) in relation to that State are extended until at least six months from publication of the IB notice (Rule 32.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successor State may fix later time limits; IB will publish such information in Official Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating availability for licensing (filing method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can file a request to indicate availability for licensing purposes by completing Form PCT/IB/382 or by a letter addressed to the International Bureau; details of licensing terms may be included. IB does not charge a fee for this service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/IB/382 is available from WIPO; applicants should send requests directly to the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing licensing indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for indication of availability for licensing purposes can be submitted at any time until the expiration of 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing relative to publication and national phases if early visibility is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple or modified licensing requests must be self-contained
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicants file multiple licensing requests or want to modify those already filed, they must ensure their latest request is always a self-contained document comprising complete information about any requests or modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on earlier filings to supply missing context — always include full, up-to-date information in the latest filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language for licensing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PCT/IB/382 will be available in the ten publication languages and the IB accepts letters in any of those languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing in one of the publication languages ensures processing and display in PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: How licensing indications are published and linked
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing of the licensing request by the IB generates a statement in the bibliographic data indicating the applicant’s interest in licensing and links to the filed request or letter, which is available under the 'Documents' tab in PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early public display of licensing indications is desired, consider filing a request for early international publication under Article 21(2)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of licensing indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can request that the IB remove the licensing indications from the 'PCT Bibliographic Data' tab in PATENTSCOPE at any time during the international or national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once removed, the licensing request and related correspondence remain part of the file history and are available under the 'Documents' tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for licensing indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing indications are a search criterion within PATENTSCOPE Search Service and can be used in combination/multi-field searches and RSS feeds to identify applicants expressing interest in licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PATENTSCOPE's search filters and RSS features to monitor licensing-available applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations system (purpose and access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may make observations through ePCT referring to prior art they believe relevant to novelty and/or inventive step of claimed inventions; there is no fee for this service (Sections 801(a), 804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ePCT (signing in without strong authentication) and consult the ePCT Third Party Observations user guide for full instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for third‑party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party observations may be submitted at any time after publication and before the expiration of 28 months from the priority date, provided the application is not withdrawn or considered withdrawn (Section 802(a)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submission falls within this window to be valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and minimum content for observations
rubrics_metrics.description: All observations must be submitted through ePCT (signing in without strong authentication). Each observation must include at least one citation to a document published before the international filing date (or a patent document with priority before the filing date) and a brief explanation of how each cited document is relevant to novelty and/or inventive step. Observations should preferably include copies of cited documents (Section 802(a)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A WIPO account is required to use ePCT. Copies help examiners but uploaded documents are not made publicly available — they are provided to applicant and competent authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity option for third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: When a third party observation is submitted, the person making the observation may indicate that they wish to remain anonymous (Section 801(b)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity is permitted, but the observation still must meet the content and citation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for third‑party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations should be submitted in a language of publication (language in which the international application was published); copies of prior art documents may be in any language (Sections 802(a)(iii), 804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting in the publication language facilitates processing; copies in other languages are acceptable for the prior art documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's right to comment on observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant will be notified about the first published observation and subsequent observations promptly after the expiration of 28 months from the priority date. The applicant may comment on third party observations until the expiration of 30 months from the priority date (Section 804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be submitted through ePCT (with strong authentication) or by letter to the IB, in English, French or the language of publication. Comments will be made publicly available on PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on third‑party observations submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may only submit a single observation for any international application, and once submitted it cannot be retracted or modified. There is an upper limit of ten observations per international application (Sections 801(b)(iii), 801(b)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submissions carefully as they are final and limited in number per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and publication of third‑party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each observation will be examined by the IB to determine if it pertains to novelty and/or inventive step and will then be made publicly available on PATENTSCOPE. Only the observations (not uploaded documents) are made publicly available. Uploaded documents are only made available to the applicant, competent International Authorities and designated Offices; if an observation is rejected the third party is notified with a reason (Sections 802(b), 803(a), 804(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations accepted by the IB are published; ensure conformity to content and timing to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and weight of third‑party observations to Authorities/Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations will be transmitted to any competent ISA and/or IPEA involved in processing the application if the IB has not yet received the ISR, SISR or IPRP. If received in time to be taken into account, prior art in observations should be considered provided a copy is included or it is immediately available to the examiner. Observations are also transmitted to designated Offices after expiration of 30 months, but designated Offices are not obliged to take them into account during national processing (Section 805).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission with copies maximizes the chance observations are considered in international reports; national Offices retain discretion in national phase.
